nodes.label: Doubtful Reports
nodes.rationale: A report is doubtful if it comes from a flagged spammer, from a visitor who reported 6 or more keys broken in a day or 4 or more across 3 or more programs, if 5 or more later visitors contradict a failure while the key works for 85 percent or more of the weighted reports, or if the tried version is newer than the latest official one.

nodes.label: Key Report Review
nodes.rationale: Last 30 days of reports, weighted by a 10-day half-life and visitor trust: spammers 0, new 0.7, returning 0.9, regular 1, star 1.2, and a visitor who reported many keys broken in a day counts half. One count per visitor per key. Suggestions need at least 3 visitors. High confidence needs 80 percent and 5 or more visitors, or 8 or more on the latest version. Failure on the latest official version while the key is listed for an older one is a reason to update the key, because most people download the latest version.

nodes.label: Analytics Schema
nodes.rationale: Visitor-driven data lives in the analytics schema. Programs, vendors, store details, and the changelog stay in Sanity. The schema is not exposed on the Data API, and RLS without policies blocks anon and authenticated. The app uses postgres.js through the Supavisor transaction pooler on port 6543 via SUPABASE_DB_URL.

nodes.label: analytics.giveaway_draws
nodes.rationale: Facebook giveaways on /admin/giveaway-picker: prizes, entrant names, and winners. It does not replace a Sanity type.

nodes.label: analytics.key_reports
nodes.rationale: Replaces Sanity keyReport and keyReportBundle.

nodes.label: analytics.legacy_documents
nodes.rationale: Keeps analyticsMigration documents verbatim.

nodes.label: prune-cron-runs Rollup Hook
nodes.rationale: The daily prune-cron-runs cron calls runAnalyticsRollup. The README describes that same job as deleting cron run logs older than 7 days.

nodes.label: analytics.prune_visitors
nodes.rationale: Deletes one-time visitors with no contributions after the raw window. Spammers and contributors are kept.

nodes.label: Analytics Rollups
nodes.rationale: Raw sessions and events are kept 30 days. daily_stats holds per-UTC-day totals, daily_sketches stores HyperLogLog sketches so multi-day unique visitors are about 3 percent off, and rollup_state.rolled_until marks completed days. Reports, comments, suggestions, contact messages, social, promo, and affiliate clicks, and pro-account copies are never deleted. A range that covers less than half of its first or last day leaves that day out. Distinct visitors across rolled days are estimates. Deleted rows do not shrink files until VACUUM FULL.

nodes.label: Sanity Analytics Migration
nodes.rationale: Until October 2026 this data lived in Sanity. It was imported on 2026-10-16 from a dataset export. Identical copies left by the old bundling cron were skipped, so totals dropped to the real numbers. origin and sanity_ref point back at the Sanity document. The import script remains only in git history.

nodes.label: analytics.sessions and events
nodes.rationale: Replace the Sanity types trackingSession and trackingSessionBundle.

nodes.label: analytics.visitors
nodes.rationale: Replaces Sanity visitor and visitorBundle. visitor_snapshots keeps older bundled copies.

nodes.label: Analytics Salt Rotation
nodes.rationale: Set ANALYTICS_SALT_PREVIOUS to the old value. On the next tracked visit a returning visitor is moved to the new hash, including the visitor row, sessions, key reports, and the ipHash on Sanity comments, replies, reactions, messages, and suggestions. Visitors who never return keep the old hash. Remove the previous salt after a few months.

nodes.label: visitor_hash
nodes.rationale: SHA-256 of the client IP plus ANALYTICS_SALT. The raw IP is never stored. The salt must stay secret and differ from NEXT_PUBLIC_ANALYTICS_SALT, because with the salt an IPv4 address can be recovered by trying every address. It is not a cookie or an account: people on one network can share a hash, and a VPN or mobile IP change creates a new one. Sessions, events, and key reports store the same hash.

nodes.label: Automation and Freshness
nodes.rationale: Describes expired-key updates, event bundling into aggregated CMS documents, and cronRun pruning around 60 days. The README prunes cron run logs after 7 days, and the Supabase notes say analytics left Sanity in October 2026. Treat the bundling and 60-day figures as possibly stale.

nodes.label: KeyAway (llms.txt)
nodes.rationale: Public site that aggregates free promotional CD keys for Windows PC utility software. Keys are community-reported and CMS-managed. It does not distribute cracks or pirated software.

nodes.label: Operator eyyMinda
nodes.rationale: Support email comes from Sanity Store Details and falls back to support@keyaway.app.

nodes.label: Hashed IP Tracking
nodes.rationale: Analytics and reports use hashed IPs and salts. Visitors have no login. Localhost traffic is typically skipped in development.

nodes.label: buildVisitorHintData
nodes.rationale: Hint copy is built in code from the tier and contributionTypeFromCounts. To edit it in Studio, add a Sanity type keyed by tier and contribution type and have buildVisitorHintData read it.

nodes.label: getVisitorContextForPublicPage
nodes.rationale: Hashes the request IP, loads the visitor from analytics.visitors, and returns visitorHint plus isSpammer.

nodes.label: isSpammerVisitor
nodes.rationale: Disables report actions on the key table. The report APIs also skip storing those reports.

nodes.label: analytics.visitors
nodes.rationale: Primary key is visitor_hash. Columns cover visit_count, last_activity_at, visit_tier, contribution counts and score, the spammer flag, and approximate country and city from the request.

nodes.label: Spammer Flag
nodes.rationale: An admin sets is_spammer from session, visitor, and comment views. Reports from a flagged visitor are accepted but not stored, except working confirmations. Public pages hide the tier hint and disable report actions.

nodes.label: Visit Tiers
nodes.rationale: analytics.visit_tier recomputes the tier in SQL on every write. resolveVisitTier in visitTier.ts is the TypeScript copy used for display. new is 1 visit or fewer, returning is 2 to 5, regular is 6 or more, and star is 16 or more visits plus a contribution score of 5 or more and not a spammer. Page views less than 30 minutes apart are one visit. Localhost tracking creates no rows. A failed upsert is logged and does not fail the request.

nodes.label: Free CD Keys and Pro Software Branding
nodes.norm_label: free cd keys and pro software branding

nodes.label: Promotion Placements
nodes.rationale: Banner text sits under the header. Card text replaces the Facebook card on program pages. A pinned row sits at the top of the bell. Popup text replaces the default bell popup. A badge can sit on the homepage hero. The button uses Button link, or the Facebook group in Store Details when that is blank. A mascot floats by the button; Banner mascot replaces it on the banner only.

nodes.label: Promotion Click Analytics
nodes.rationale: Clicks are social_click events with social set to promo-banner, promo-program, promo-bell, or promo-home, and label set to the promotion id. Conversion is the visitors who clicked, out of everyone active during the campaign.

nodes.label: sitePromotion
nodes.rationale: Temporary giveaway and sale campaigns, including Halloween, Christmas, and Black Friday presets, or a duplicate of last year. Changes appear after the revalidation webhook, otherwise within 12 hours. Everything disappears at Ends with no redeploy. Turn off Enabled and publish to stop sooner.

nodes.label: Analytics
nodes.rationale: Page views, key copies, downloads, and shares are keyed by a salted IP hash, never the raw IP. sync-program-stats every 6 hours rolls sessions into per-program counts that drive popularity sorting and the featured-program rotation.

nodes.label: Changelog Sync
nodes.rationale: Merged pull requests become /changelog entries. A GitHub Action runs scripts/syncChangelogPrToSanity.mjs to turn the PR description into a Sanity release document.

nodes.label: KeyAway
nodes.rationale: Free working giveaway CD keys and PRO accounts for Windows and Mac software, kept current. One-person production app: a Next.js public site, a Sanity studio, an admin dashboard, and cron jobs that find giveaways, track versions, and keep keys honest.

nodes.label: Sanity CMS
nodes.rationale: Sanity v5 holds editorial content. Studio is embedded at /studio.

nodes.label: Supabase Postgres
nodes.rationale: High-volume analytics (sessions, events, visitors, key reports) live in Supabase Postgres, accessed with the postgres driver. Migrations in supabase/migrations are applied once in the SQL editor.

nodes.label: clipPath a
nodes.rationale: defs holds clipPath id a. Its path is M0 0h16v16H0z, a 16 by 16 rectangle, fill #fff.

nodes.label: Clipped group
nodes.rationale: The g element sets clip-path to url(#a), binding the globe path to clipPath a.

nodes.label: Globe compound path
nodes.rationale: One path with fill-rule evenodd, clip-rule evenodd, and fill #666. Subpaths are the disc, southern cap, right meridian, equatorial band, northeast gore, northern cap, northwest gore, left meridian, and southwest gore.

nodes.label: svg
nodes.rationale: Root element. xmlns is http://www.w3.org/2000/svg. fill is none, so only the path fill paints. viewBox is 0 0 16 16.

nodes.label: Globe disc
nodes.rationale: Subpath M8 16 A8 8 0 1 0 8 0 a8 8 0 0 0 0 16 is a circle of radius 8 centered at (8, 8).
The globe path is filled #666. The clip-path rectangle is filled #fff and only defines the clip shape.

nodes.label: Globe graticule
nodes.rationale: Latitude bands: northern cap at M8.48 1.5, southern cap offset (.48, -1.52) from (8, 16), each with a radius-40 arc spanning 3.92; equatorial loop of width 4.3 and height 3.64 using radii 17 and 39. Meridians: left from M4.58 6.28 and the matching right strip (radii 7 and 18), plus four corner gores on radius-6.5 arcs.

nodes.label: Globe Icon
nodes.rationale: The single compound path is a world-globe mark: a radius-8 disc, polar caps, an equatorial band, and meridian gores. It is filled #666 and clipped to the 16 by 16 viewBox.

nodes.label: evenodd fill and clip rules
nodes.rationale: fill-rule evenodd and clip-rule evenodd make the overlapping graticule subpaths cut the disc so the latitude and meridian bands read as the globe grid.

nodes.label: __sanityErrorChannel
nodes.rationale: Only subscribe is placed on window so the app can listen. If subscribers exist, the error is published and not logged or overlaid. Events with no error object, such as a ResizeObserver loop or a cross-origin Script error, are ignored.

nodes.label: Sanity Studio Shell
nodes.rationale: Auto-generated by sanity dev; edits are discarded. The page is noindex, mounts #sanity, and loads /.sanity/runtime/app.js plus the Sanity bridge. A noscript fallback tells the user to enable JavaScript.

nodes.label: window.onerror
nodes.rationale: Returns true so the browser console does not also render the error. Duplicate throws are dropped with a short-lived _caughtErrors list.

nodes.label: React Dev Double Throw
nodes.rationale: Two error listeners are attached because React throws the same error twice in development. See facebook/react issue 10384.

nodes.label: applyKeyStatusForDisplay
nodes.rationale: Program pages apply status rules before render so a key that expired an hour ago already shows as expired, even when Sanity has not been updated. Nothing is written on page load.

nodes.label: Key Status Rules
nodes.rationale: A past validUntil moves a non-expired entry to expired. Status new becomes active when createdAt, else validFrom, is older than 30 days. An empty validUntil is a lifetime key. limit is set by hand or from visitor reports when activations run out. Display applies the rules in memory and does not write; the nightly job persists the same rules.

nodes.label: update-expired-keys
nodes.rationale: POST /api/v1/cron/update-expired-keys runs at 22:00 UTC. It accepts an admin session or Authorization Bearer CRON_SECRET. Each run is a cronRun document on the admin dashboard.

nodes.label: Giveaway Finder
nodes.rationale: Scans configured giveaway sites only for programs KeyAway already lists. Matching ignores edition words, versions, and vendor prefixes. Only matching posts are opened. Crawling respects robots.txt, per-host limits, and page-size caps.

nodes.label: Scheduled Cron Jobs
nodes.rationale: vercel.json schedules sync-program-stats every 6 hours, check-versions at 06:00 UTC, discover-giveaways at 07:00, update-expired-keys at 22:00, and prune-cron-runs at 03:15, which deletes cron run logs older than 7 days. Routes accept the Vercel cron header or Bearer CRON_SECRET.

nodes.label: Version Checks
nodes.rationale: Best source is the vendor installer: the first megabyte of the vendor exe, same-day and first-party, and it flags web-installer stubs. Then the vendor page, FilePuma, and winget, Chocolatey, and Homebrew. Versions compare as major.minor. The daily job writes only when a result changes.

nodes.label: Prefill Vendor
nodes.rationale: Produces a vendor PrefillResult (hub description, aliases, giveaway key versus official PRO, SEO, logo) for the admin vendor Prefill dialog. Nothing is written to Sanity from the command. Gaps come only from the vendor's own site.

nodes.label: Document Page
nodes.rationale: Outer contour runs from the top-left at x 1.5 across a clipped top-right corner to y 5.41, down the right edge to y 13.5, then 2.5-radius arcs along the bottom at y 16. The next subpath insets that outline so the even-odd fill leaves a gray border and an empty page face.

nodes.label: Folded Corner
nodes.rationale: Triangle subpath M9.5 5 V2.12 L12.38 5 z sits in the clipped top-right of the page.

nodes.label: Text Lines
nodes.rationale: Three horizontal bars on the page face, each 1.25 tall. The top bar is short (about 2.12 wide, y 5 to 6.25). The middle bar (y 8 to 9.25) and bottom bar (y 11 to 12.25) span about 7.12.

nodes.label: file.svg
nodes.rationale: 16 by 16 SVG icon. viewBox 0 0 16 16, root fill none, one path filled #666 with fill-rule and clip-rule evenodd.

nodes.label: Even-Odd Compound Fill
nodes.rationale: fill-rule evenodd on the single path knocks out the inner contour so the page face stays empty, then the dog-ear and the three bars fill #666 again because they lie inside that hole.

nodes.label: Public Verification Token
nodes.rationale: The file body is the single token c2ead36245bf40d2b1f28d4b3ec68d09.

nodes.label: Official Press Kit
nodes.rationale: IObit's press room is found automatically. A press-kit zip or press page can be passed. Screenshot references of the form presskit are used as about-section images when they match the section.

nodes.label: PROGRAM_RESULT_SHAPE
nodes.rationale: Output kind is program. latestOfficialVersion is major.minor only. Category names must come from the scraper list. Markdown is used in text fields.

nodes.label: Vendor Installer Version
nodes.rationale: The version read from the vendor's own exe and its file date is the most reliable version and release date. versionCheck uses source installer when an installer was found, otherwise source page.

nodes.label: FilePuma Version Source
nodes.rationale: Searches GlarySoft FilePuma by exact program name. Requests are spaced 5 seconds apart because of its robots.txt. It can lag the vendor by a release. Used when there is no installer source.

nodes.label: Installer Version Source
nodes.rationale: Reads the version from the first 1 MB of the vendor exe via HTTP Range, from a Mac pkg Distribution file, or from an exe inside a zip up to 40 MB. Last-Modified is the release date. Used when the vendor publishes a direct installer, such as IObit, iTop, MacBooster, and iCare.

nodes.label: Package Catalog Version Sources
nodes.rationale: winget reads the highest version folder in microsoft/winget-pkgs; GITHUB_TOKEN raises the GitHub rate limit. Chocolatey and Homebrew are fallbacks, and Homebrew is for Mac apps.

nodes.label: Page Version Source
nodes.rationale: Takes the highest Version x.y on the page, or a custom regex with one capture group. Used when the installer is a small web-installer stub, such as SoftOrbits.

nodes.label: Admin Prefill
nodes.rationale: Each content group can be applied on its own, and groups that already have content start unticked. About sections keep images already in place. Images are copied into Sanity. Nothing is saved until Save. Claude Code /prefill-program and /prefill-vendor use the same sources and rules, write git-ignored JSON, and do not write to Sanity.

nodes.label: pressKit
nodes.rationale: Accepts a zip URL, a kit linked from a press page, or IObit's press room, where the newest kit for the product is picked. Unzipped in memory. Screenshots are referenced as presskit:zip#file and the image import route copies them into Sanity on apply.

nodes.label: PROGRAM_WRITING_RULES
nodes.rationale: buildProgramPrompt sends the sources, these rules, the JSON shape, and the page's current content so the model improves the page instead of starting over. parsePrefillResult accepts the answer with or without a code fence.

nodes.label: scrapePage
nodes.rationale: Reads metadata, JSON-LD, feature sections, FAQs, download links, version text, and images. Menus, headers, and seasonal promo images are stripped. FAQs come from FAQPage JSON-LD, details, dl, and question-style headings. IObit pages also use the product section of iobit.com/en/allfaq.php.

nodes.label: Version Checks
nodes.rationale: versionCheck stores the source, URL or package id, and auto-apply. versionStatus is written only by the check. Found versions are trimmed to major.minor and count as new only when higher than latestOfficialVersion. The daily job checks four programs at a time and applies the version only when auto-apply is on. A file under 2.5 MB or named online or downloader is a web-installer stub whose version belongs to the downloader, not the program.

nodes.label: Program Prefill
nodes.rationale: Building a program page by hand is slow, so Prefill gathers the vendor page, official press kit, and installer first. Facts can be applied as-is or returned as JSON from an AI prompt. Nothing is saved until the form is reviewed. Writing rules: no hype, no duplicated claims, only sourced facts.

nodes.label: Prefill Program
nodes.rationale: Produces one program PrefillResult for Admin, Programs, Prefill, AI result. Nothing is written to Sanity from the command; the user pastes, reviews, and saves. Prefer installer and press-kit facts over marketing copy, and fill gaps only from the vendor's own site.

nodes.label: Suggestion and Contact Storage
nodes.rationale: Name, email, and message or key details are stored in Sanity for administrators only, and kept until processed. Only the CD key is published. The email is used only to reply.

nodes.label: Program Editor
nodes.rationale: Rich text is edited as Markdown. A field whose Markdown was not changed is saved as its original Portable Text. PATCH sends rev plus only the changed fields. ifRevisionId returns 409 when Studio, a cron, or another tab changed the document, and the editor offers to reload. After save, cache tags are invalidated, the header notification feed is rebuilt, and IndexNow is pinged. An FAQ needs 0 or at least 2 items, and there are at most 4 about sections.

nodes.label: Programs Table
nodes.rationale: GET /api/v1/admin/programs loads rows on the server because vendor ids such as vendor.iobit are private in Sanity and a browser query cannot see them. Filtering and sorting happen in the browser. Expanded rows show only working keys. The open editor is stored in the URL so refresh and history work.

nodes.label: Vendors Editor
nodes.rationale: A vendor can be deleted only when no program uses it. Aliases feed the giveaway scanner. The editor includes the giveaway-key versus official PRO rows.

nodes.label: User Contributions
nodes.rationale: Contributors may suggest legitimate giveaway keys, report working, expired, or limit reached, and comment. KeyAway may moderate, verify, or remove submissions. Submitted keys may be published after verification.

nodes.label: Admin and Studio
nodes.rationale: Studio at /studio edits programs, keys, store copy, and social links. /admin is OAuth with an allowlist for analytics, raw events, programs, key reports, suggestions, messages, and featured programs.

nodes.label: Notification Feed
nodes.rationale: GET /api/v1/notifications/recent reads the rebuilt siteNotificationFeed, one entry per program inside about 30 days, instead of a live query over every program.

nodes.label: Public API v1
nodes.rationale: Public routes cover analytics track, notifications recent, key reports, key suggestions, and contact. Cron and webhook routes are not a general third-party API.

nodes.label: Admin Auth
nodes.rationale: Auth.js (NextAuth v5) with GitHub, optional Google, and an email allowlist. Google is enabled by setting AUTH_GOOGLE_ID and AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET and uncommenting the provider in auth.ts.

nodes.label: Admin Dashboard
nodes.rationale: GitHub sign-in is limited to ADMIN_ALLOWED_EMAILS or Sanity project members. Admin APIs live under /api/v1/admin and check the session on the server.

nodes.label: Cache Tag Revalidation
nodes.rationale: Public pages are cached for 12 hours and invalidated earlier by tag so the site stays fast without going stale. Admin saves and the Sanity revalidation webhook bust the affected tags.

nodes.label: Program and Vendor Editor
nodes.rationale: Saves send only changed fields and are rejected if the document changed since it was opened. Untouched rich text is saved byte for byte. Markdown round-trips to Sanity Portable Text without losing formatting.

nodes.label: siteNotificationFeed
nodes.rationale: One document powers the header bell. It is rebuilt whenever programs or keys change.

nodes.label: Advertising Consent
nodes.rationale: In the EEA, the UK, and Switzerland, advertising cookies are used only after acceptance. Elsewhere ads load by default and can be opted out. Your privacy choices in the footer reopens the choice. A Global Privacy Control signal is an opt-out in every region. Contact details, comments, and messages are not passed to advertisers.

nodes.label: Affiliate and Outbound Links
nodes.rationale: Following a vendor download, upgrade, or banner leaves KeyAway. Some links may be affiliate links. Purchases happen on the vendor site. Key status reports collect no personal data.

nodes.label: One-way IP Hash
nodes.rationale: The IP is never stored as-is. It becomes a one-way code that cannot be turned back into the address and cannot pinpoint location. A temporary visit ID lives in the browser tab and clears when the tab closes. Detailed records are kept up to 12 months, then only aggregates such as view counts and top countries. The basis is legitimate interest in running and protecting the site. Personal data is not sold or shared with advertisers.

nodes.label: Affiliate Disclosure
nodes.rationale: There is no checkout on keyaway.app. Some outbound download, upgrade, or banner links are affiliate links; a purchase on the vendor site may earn a commission at no extra cost. Prices stay with the vendor. Labeled third-party ads are not endorsements. These arrangements keep listings free. Copying a listed giveaway key does not require a purchase.

nodes.label: Donations
nodes.rationale: Donations are voluntary and non-refundable and are used only to operate and host the site.

nodes.label: Key Validity
nodes.rationale: Giveaway keys may be version-specific and time-limited. Availability after the distributor ends the promotion is not guaranteed. The site is provided as-is and is not liable for invalid, expired, or misused keys.

nodes.label: Affiliate Links and Ads
nodes.rationale: KeyAway does not operate a store. Outbound vendor links may be affiliate links. Labeled third-party ads fund the site, are not endorsements, and no content requires clicking an ad.

nodes.label: Activation Entries
nodes.rationale: Each program lists CD keys, PRO accounts, or giveaway links, depending on its activation flow.

nodes.label: Ads and Consent
nodes.rationale: Units load near the viewport and only with ad consent. Opt-in for the EEA, UK, and Switzerland; opt-out elsewhere. Global Privacy Control is honored. Ads never load in admin or Studio. New ad domains must be added to AD_ORIGINS in the Content Security Policy.

nodes.label: Key Status
nodes.rationale: Statuses are new, working, expired, and limit reached. Keys past validUntil show as expired when the page renders and are saved expired by a nightly job. New keys become active after 30 days.

nodes.label: Public Giveaway Keys
nodes.rationale: Listed CD keys are public giveaway keys from software distributors, aggregated so they are easier to find. No stolen, pirated, or unauthorized keys are hosted or distributed.

nodes.label: No Pirated Keys
nodes.rationale: KeyAway does not host, distribute, or promote pirated or stolen keys. Its role is to make legitimate distributor giveaway keys easier to discover in one place.
